data.text:
## app-shell — App shell (pattern, archetype navigate)
The persistent frame around an application’s content: global navigation, identity, search, and the region where content changes.
Aliases: application frame, chrome, navigation shell, scaffold
Anatomy: Global navigation (Top-level destinations); Top bar (Title, search and account); Content region (Where destinations render); Secondary navigation (Destinations within a destination)
Related — uses: tabs, drawer, menu, badge, breadcrumbs, tree-view | specializes: navigate | neighbors: split-pane, command-palette
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Navigation placement [layout] — Where are primary and secondary navigation?
  - primary (single-select: one id) — Primary navigation
      top-navigation-bar: Top navigation bar (e.g. GitHub)
      sidebar: Sidebar (e.g. Notion)
      navigation-rail: Navigation rail (e.g. Material 3 rail on tablets)
      bottom-tab-bar: Bottom tab bar (e.g. Instagram)
      drawer: Drawer (e.g. Gmail on Android)
      tab-bar-that-expands-to-sidebar: Tab bar that expands to sidebar (e.g. iPadOS 18 tab bar)
  - secondary (single-select: one id) — Secondary navigation
      none: None (e.g. Instagram)
      second-sidebar-column: Second sidebar column (e.g. Discord channel list beside the server rail)
      sub-tabs-under-the-header: Sub-tabs under the header (e.g. GitHub repository tabs)
      contextual-panel: Contextual panel (e.g. Settings sub-pages)
* Navigation items [content] — What does navigation contain, and how does it change?
  - items (multi-select: list of ids) — Items
      fixed-destinations: Fixed destinations (e.g. Instagram tabs)
      user-pinned-items: User-pinned items (e.g. Notion favourites)
      recents: Recents (e.g. Figma recents)
      live-counts: Live counts — Unread or pending badges (e.g. Slack unreads)
      workspace-switcher: Workspace switcher (e.g. Discord server rail)
* Show and hide [invocation] — Is the shell always there?
  - visibility (single-select: one id) — Visibility
      always-visible: Always visible (e.g. Slack)
      toggle-button: Toggle button (e.g. Gmail collapse menu)
      collapse-on-scroll: Collapse on scroll (e.g. Safari on iOS toolbar)
      reveal-on-hover: Reveal on hover (e.g. Edge vertical tabs collapsed)
* Responsive shell [adaptation] — What happens as the screen narrows?
  - narrowing (single-select: one id) — Narrowing
      collapse-to-icons: Collapse to icons (e.g. Gmail icon rail)
      become-bottom-tabs: Become bottom tabs (e.g. Cross-platform apps)
      become-drawer: Become drawer (e.g. Material responsive layouts)
      hide-in-immersive-mode: Hide in immersive mode (e.g. Full-screen reading and video)
* Workspace structure [composition] — How many applications or workspaces does one shell hold?
  - structure (single-select: one id) — Structure
      single-app: Single app (e.g. Most apps)
      multi-workspace-rail: Multi-workspace rail (e.g. Discord servers)
      mini-apps-inside-an-app: Mini-apps inside an app (e.g. WeChat Mini Programs)
      document-tabs: Document tabs (e.g. Browsers, Figma file tabs)

## menu — Menu (component, archetype navigate)
A transient list of choices or commands revealed from a trigger.
Aliases: dropdown menu, context menu, overflow menu, menu bar, mega menu
Anatomy: Trigger (What opens the menu); Items (Choices and commands); Structure (Sections and submenus)
Related — neighbors: command-palette, popover
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Opening [invocation] — What opens it?
  - openBy (single-select: one id) — Opened by
      button-click: Button click (e.g. Overflow ⋮ menus)
      right-click-or-long-press: Right-click or long-press (e.g. Context menus)
      menu-bar: Menu bar (e.g. macOS menu bar)
      hover: Hover (e.g. Retail mega menus)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. Alt to reach Windows menus)
* Structure [composition] — How are items organized?

data.name: get_patterns
data.text:
## accordion — Accordion (component, archetype browse-collections)
Stacked sections whose headers expand to reveal their content in place.
Aliases: disclosure, collapsible sections, expander
Anatomy: Header (The always-visible label); Panel (The revealed content); Indicator (Chevron or plus)
Related — specializes: overview-detail | neighbors: tabs, tree-view
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Expansion policy [scope] — How many sections can be open?
  - policy (single-select: one id) — Open at once
      one-at-a-time: One at a time — Opening one closes the others (e.g. ESPN player stats)
      many-at-a-time: Many at a time — Sections open independently (e.g. weather.com hourly details)
      all-open-by-default: All open by default (e.g. Printable FAQs)
* Header content [content] — What does a closed section say about what is inside?
  - header (multi-select: list of ids) — Header content
      title-only: Title only (e.g. FAQ pages)
      title-plus-summary-value: Title plus summary value (e.g. Checkout order summary)
      status-indicator: Status indicator (e.g. Settings sections showing errors)
* Toggle [invocation] — How is a section opened?
  - toggle (multi-select: list of ids) — Toggle by
      header-click: Header click (e.g. Most accordions)
      indicator-only: Indicator only (e.g. Tree-like panels)
      expand-all-control: Expand all control (e.g. Documentation sites)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. WAI-ARIA accordion pattern)
* Memory [lifecycle] — Does it remember what was open?
  - memory (single-select: one id) — State memory
      resets: Resets (e.g. Most web pages)
      per-session: Per session (e.g. Single-page apps)
      persists: Persists (e.g. IDE side panels)

## badge — Badge (component, archetype monitor)
A small indicator on another element showing a count or a status.
Aliases: counter, notification dot, status pill
Anatomy: Host (What it is attached to); Indicator (Count, dot or label)
Related — neighbors: stat-tile, progress-indicator
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Meaning [content] — What does the badge say?
  - meaning (single-select: one id) — Meaning
      count: Count (e.g. Unread messages)
      dot: Dot — Something new (e.g. App icon dots)
      status: Status (e.g. Online presence)
      label: Label (e.g. New or Beta)
* Overflow [encoding] — How are large counts shown?
  - overflow (single-select: one id) — Overflow
      exact-count: Exact count (e.g. Mail folders)
      capped: Capped — 99+ (e.g. Many apps)
      dot-past-a-threshold: Dot past a threshold (e.g. Minimal badges)
* What counts [initiative] — Who decides what increments it?
  - rule (single-select: one id) — Counting rule
      everything-unread: Everything unread (e.g. Default mail badges)
      only-mentions: Only mentions (e.g. Slack mentions-only badge setting)
      the-person-s-rule: The person’s rule (e.g. Custom inbox counts)
      pending-actions: Pending actions — The badge counts work waiting for the person — updates to install, apps to update, tasks to finish — rather than anything read, unread or addressed to them; the counting rules as written assume a message inbox (e.g. iOS Settings — App icon)
* Aggregation [scope] — Does it roll up?
  - aggregation (single-select: one id) — Aggregation
      per-item: Per item (e.g. Folder counts)
      rolled-up-to-parent: Rolled up to parent (e.g. Account totals)
      app-icon-total: App icon total (e.g. iOS app badges)
      device-total: Device total — One indicator for every unread notification on the device, on system chrome rather than on any app's icon or nav entry (watch faces, always-on displays) (e.g. Apple Watch — Watch face)
